findings.evidence: Grep hits: `ExponentialShift.lean:39:@[expose] def expShift`, `:64:theorem expShift_apply`, `:97:theorem expShift_realOperator_of_nonneg`, `:127:theorem expShift ...`.
findings.fix: Remove `@[expose]` from `expShift`; keep downstream proofs using `expShift_apply`, `expShift_realOperator_of_nonneg`, and `HasGrowthBound.expShift` instead of definitional unfolding.
findings.issue: `StronglyContinuousSemigroup.expShift` is marked `@[expose]`, making the semigroup constructor body part of the public API even though the file already exports `@[simp] theorem expShift_apply` and real-time formulas for use without unfolding.

findings.fix: Remove `@[expose]` from `expShiftContraction`; consumers should use `expShiftContraction_toStronglyContinuousSemigroup` and `expShiftContraction_apply`.
findings.issue: `StronglyContinuousSemigroup.expShiftContraction` is also marked `@[expose]`, exposing the bundled `ContractionSemigroup` construction when the public coercion and native-operator lemmas already characterize it.

summary: The new exponential-shift API is useful and has characteristic lemmas, but it exposes constructor bodies that downstream users do not need to unfold. Keep the public interface lemma-driven and make these definitions opaque.
